```markdown
# Roadmap — SEC filing-index ingestion

## Outcomes

Source: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec.md. Background: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-adr.md.
Choices made: Python 3.14 (`.python-version`). uv workspace of four member packages (root `pyproject.toml`).

| # | Outcome | Spec | Track | Rank | Cost (estimate; basis) |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| O1 | Archived quarterly filing indexes for a configured quarter range, downloaded and parsed | R1; §2.1, §4.2 Backfill | A | 1 | Requests are small: about 2 per quarter, and up to about 135 quarters if the range starts at 1993 Q1, where the full-index archive begins; at 3 req/s (§4.8) that is minutes. Bytes and time are measured by Stage 1 |
| O2 | Daily filing indexes ingested on an ongoing basis, catching up after missed runs | R2; §4.2 Daily ingestion | A | 2 | About 250 daily indexes a year, one request each plus listings (§4.2); size measured by Stage 2 |
| O3 | A canonical filing-index dataset in Parquet, built from the ingested indexes | R3; §4.5 row contract, §4.6 | A | 3 | Compute measured by Stage 1 |
| O4 | The ingestion running on Azure (ADF, Container Apps Jobs, ADLS, Table Storage, Monitor) | R4; §4.1, §4.9 | A | 4 | Azure spend cannot be estimated before deployment (§2.2); measured by Stage 7 |
| O5 | Backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation sharing one downloader, parser and publisher | R5; §4.1 | A | 5 | Not material |
| O6 | Original index bytes kept, so a parser change reprocesses without downloading again | R6; §4.3, §4.5 | A | 6 | Storage equals the raw bytes of O1 and O2; measured by Stages 1–2 |
| O7 | Quarterly indexes re-read on a schedule, with additions and changed fields recorded | R7; §4.2 Reconciliation, §4.4 | A | 7 | Each run makes about as many requests as O1 (§4.2) |
| O8 | All SEC traffic sent through one downloader under one request budget | R8; §4.3 | A | 8 | Not material; traffic is capped at 3 req/s (§4.8) |
| O9 | Readers find the current dataset through one versioned pointer per quarter | R9; §4.5, §4.6 | A | 9 | Storage grows by one generation per changed quarter; retention is set in Stage 7 |
| O10 | Closed-quarter withdrawals published only after an approval bound to the source hash | R10; §4.4 | A | 10 | Your partner's time per approval; frequency unknown until Stage 8 runs |
| O11 | The starting schedules, retry limits and rate target held as reviewed, validated configuration | R11; §4.8, §5 Configuration | A | 11 | Not material |

Tracks: A — SEC filing-index ingestion (known progression).

## Open questions

1. Package layout. §4.9 puts all code in `packages/sec-edgar-ingest`. The repository instead has four scaffolds (`sec-edgar-client`, `sec-edgar-download`, `sec-edgar-index-ingest`, `sec-edgar-ingest`), plus a root `sec-edgar` script that points to a `sec_edgar` module that does not exist. Settle this in Stage 1's brainstorming.
2. Acceptance. The ADR and the spec are both still Proposed. §7 step 1 requires them to be accepted before deployment. Stages 1–6 do not depend on Azure. Stage 7 consumes the acceptance.

## Stages

- [ ] Stage 1: Local quarterly backfill core
      Objective: Download archived quarterly master indexes for a configured range from the SEC and write them as canonical Parquet rows on local disk.
      Outcomes: O1, O3
      Consumes: nothing
      Produces: a parser that emits `sec-index-v1` rows, a CLI entry point, and the package layout settled (Open question 1); specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-stage-1-findings.md
      Exit: O1: one real archived quarter is downloaded with an identifying User-Agent at no more than 3 req/s. O3: its rows are written as Parquet that meets the §4.5 row contract, with the row count matching the source. The run also records byte count, elapsed time, peak memory, request count and observed request rate.
      Leaves out: source manifest and replay: Stage 3; shared request budget: Stage 4; versioned publication: Stage 5; Azure deployment: Stage 7; scheduling, monitoring and runbooks: Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 2: Daily ingestion and catch-up
      Objective: Discover and ingest daily master indexes from `index.json` listings, through the same downloader and parser, with pending and failed sources tracked.
      Outcomes: O2
      Consumes: Stage 1 downloader, parser and CLI
      Produces: discovery state that survives across runs; daily rows in the same contract
      Exit: O2: one already-published real daily index is ingested. On fixtures, a missed run and an outage spanning several quarters both catch up, and a failed listing does not advance the boundary.
      Leaves out: source manifest and replay: Stage 3; shared request budget: Stage 4; versioned publication: Stage 5; scheduling, monitoring and runbooks: Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 3: Source manifest and replay
      Objective: Keep the original bytes content-addressed, and keep observations keyed by snapshot, parser and schema, with manifest records for each source, snapshot and processing step.
      Outcomes: O6
      Consumes: Stages 1–2 collection and parsing
      Produces: the raw and observation stores and source-manifest records (§4.5)
      Exit: O6: a parser-version change rebuilds output from stored bytes with SEC access disabled, unchanged hashes skip the work, and a partly complete run resumes without losing finished units.
      Leaves out: versioned publication: Stage 5; Azure deployment: Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 4: Shared request budget and configuration
      Objective: Send every SEC request through one leased, throttled downloader with the bounded retry policy, and validate configuration before any external I/O.
      Outcomes: O8, O11
      Consumes: the Stages 1–3 downloader
      Produces: a request-budget lease and a typed config (§4.8), both used by every later caller
      Exit: O8: concurrent collectors on fixtures never overlap as request issuers; retries count toward the budget; Retry-After is honored; access denial halts the run. O11: each invalid setting in §5 Configuration is refused before any network request.
      Leaves out: Azure deployment: Stage 7
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 5: Versioned publication
      Objective: Publish each quarter as an immutable generation with a manifest and change report, made current by a conditional pointer update.
      Outcomes: O9
      Consumes: Stage 3 observations and manifest
      Produces: generations and an active pointer per quarter that readers resolve (§4.6)
      Exit: O9: with crashes injected before the files finish, before the pointer update and just after it, readers only ever see complete generations, and competing publishers lose no update.
      Leaves out: Azure deployment: Stage 7
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 6: Reconciliation and withdrawal gate
      Objective: Re-read quarterly indexes through the shared commands and apply the precedence and withdrawal rules in §4.4.
      Outcomes: O7, O10, O5
      Consumes: Stages 3–5
      Produces: change records and approval records (§4.5)
      Exit: O7: additions and field updates are recorded, and absence from an open quarter withdraws nothing. O10: a closed-quarter removal stays `awaiting_approval` until an approval naming its hash, and stale daily replays cannot bring back a withdrawn key. O5: backfill, daily ingestion and reconciliation differ only in source selection.
      Leaves out: scheduling, monitoring and runbooks: Stage 8
      ROUTING: writing-plans

- [ ] Stage 7: Azure deployment
      Objective: Run the shared worker on the R4 platform in an isolated environment, with infrastructure as code, managed identities and production triggers disabled.
      Outcomes: O4
      Consumes: Stages 1–6; the ADR and spec accepted (Open question 2)
      Produces: a deployed image and configuration in an isolated environment
      Exit: O4: integration tests (§6) pass on isolated Azure resources; the §7 step 4 smoke test and the step 5 replay both pass; the measured Azure cost of those runs is recorded.
      Leaves out: scheduling, monitoring and runbooks: Stage 8
      ROUTING: brainstorming

- [ ] Stage 8: Scheduling, monitoring and runbooks
      Objective: Add alerts, run reports and runbooks, then run the full baseline, the daily catch-up and the first reconciliation, and enable the triggers (§7 Phase 2).
      Outcomes: O1 (full range), O2 (scheduled), O7 (scheduled)
      Consumes: Stage 7 deployment
      Produces: a release record naming image and configuration versions and the active generations
      Exit: O1: every requested baseline unit is published, or the incomplete range is recorded as approved. O2: observed scheduled daily runs, with their reports and logs. O7: an observed scheduled reconciliation, with its gated candidates resolved.
      Leaves out: nothing
      ROUTING: brainstorming

## Stage-spec stamp

> Roadmap: specs/sec-filing-index-ingestion-spec-roadmap.md, Stage N — on plan completion, tick the
> stage and re-validate later stages against what shipped.

## Completion

When every stage is ticked, re-run the gap rubric over O1–O11, with evidence per verdict (the implementing stage and plan, Deviation notes, deferred items). Then list as unmet any numbered spec requirement (R1–R11) that no outcome's Spec cell cites. Each unmet item leaves one of two ways: a new stage, or a deferral with a written reason.
```

---

The order follows your ranking except in two places: O3 joins Stage 1 to make the core usable, and O4 (Azure) moves to Stage 7 because it depends on working code and on accepting the ADR. Do you approve this eight-stage partition as written, or what would you change?
